headline: 32,000 schools: No legal bar to appointing head teachers
summary: The Supreme Court has removed the final legal hurdle for headteacher appointments in approximately 32,500 government primary schools.
details: The Supreme Court has ended a long-running dispute over the seniority and promotion of teachers absorbed into the government primary education system.
A four-member Appellate Division bench, led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, delivered the ruling on Thursday.
The case originated from a conflict between directly recruited teachers and those whose schools were nationalised, specifically regarding seniority and promotion rules.
Under 2013 recruitment rules, teachers absorbed through nationalisation were placed below the last directly recruited teacher in the seniority list.
A group of 383 nationalised teachers challenged this policy, and the High Court Division had previously declared the provision illegal.
This High Court ruling had caused headmaster appointments to grind to a halt across 32,500 primary institutions.
However, the Appellate Division has now overturned the High Court's decision, leaving the 2013 seniority provision intact.
Consequently, teachers absorbed after nationalisation will continue to rank below directly recruited teachers in the seniority list, clearing the way for appointments.
caption:
Headteacher appointments in 32,500 government primary schools are finally moving forward after a Supreme Court ruling.

The Supreme Court has ended a long-running dispute over the seniority and promotion of teachers absorbed into the government primary education system.

A four-member Appellate Division bench, led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, delivered the ruling on Thursday.

The case originated from a conflict between directly recruited teachers and those whose schools were nationalised, specifically regarding seniority and promotion rules.

Under 2013 recruitment rules, teachers absorbed through nationalisation were placed below the last directly recruited teacher in the seniority list.

A group of 383 nationalised teachers challenged this policy, and the High Court Division had previously declared the provision illegal.

This High Court ruling had caused headmaster appointments to grind to a halt across 32,500 primary institutions.

However, the Appellate Division has now overturned the High Court's decision, leaving the 2013 seniority provision intact.

Consequently, teachers absorbed after nationalisation will continue to rank below directly recruited teachers in the seniority list, clearing the way for appointments.

headline: Parliament Speaker leaves for Iran to attend funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
summary: Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed departed from Dhaka on Thursday morning to pay his final respects to the Iranian Supreme Leader.
details: Bangladesh National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed left Dhaka on Thursday morning to attend the funeral of Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
He departed from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 7:30 AM on July 2, and is expected to return to the country on July 4.
Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was born on April 19, 1939, in Mashhad, northeastern Iran, and passed away on February 28, 2026, at the age of 86.
He played a pivotal role in the new governance system following the 1979 Islamic Revolution in Iran.
Khamenei served as a brief tenure as Defense Minister in 1980 and later as the supervisor of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps during the Iran-Iraq War.
Following the death of Ruhollah Khomeini in 1989, the Assembly of Experts elected him as the Supreme Leader of Iran.
caption:
Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed departs for Iran to attend the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Bangladesh National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed left Dhaka on Thursday morning to attend the funeral of Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

He departed from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 7:30 AM on July 2, and is expected to return to the country on July 4.

Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was born on April 19, 1939, in Mashhad, northeastern Iran, and passed away on February 28, 2026, at the age of 86.

He played a pivotal role in the new governance system following the 1979 Islamic Revolution in Iran.

Khamenei served as a brief tenure as Defense Minister in 1980 and later as the supervisor of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps during the Iran-Iraq War.

Following the death of Ruhollah Khomeini in 1989, the Assembly of Experts elected him as the Supreme Leader of Iran.
